fields.description:
## Context / Problem
Bugs are exempt from the claim-time plan-review gate (correct: no RCA exists at claim), and since epic 6982/R4 an explicit 'review-plan <bug>' is no longer a hollow exempt-PASS — it runs the LIGHT ADVISORY bug tier: the DET floor + the necessity probe only (workflow_ops.py bug branch; registry.BUG_TIER_CRITERIA restricts the LLM criteria), with every DET finding downgraded to advisory (det_blocking=[]) so a bug always PASSes. That tier is right-sized for small fixes but means a complex fix plan is never substantively reviewed against the full rubric before landing — fixes shipping design changes (backtest: 13/113 bug-fix commits exceeded 150 non-test lines; all 13 adjudicated substantive, two shipped ADRs) flow to main with at most advisory findings.

## Approach
B1 (extend the bug review tier, not narrow an exemption): in the workflow_ops.py bug branch + orchestrator.route_criteria (~:190) — the SINGLE routing seam that keys the bug tier (registry.BUG_TIER_CRITERIA restriction at ~:221) and is reached by BOTH the assemble step and the batch-runner's project-criteria fan-in, so escalation lands once and covers both callers —, key the tier on the ticket's PERSISTED declared blast radius, derived DETERMINISTICALLY at review time (no diff exists yet): escalate iff the ticket's recorded file_impact enumerates any non-test path (tests/**, conftest.py excluded). file_impact lives in ticket state, which BOTH enforcement steps already read — plan_review_precheck (workflow_ops.py ~:115, which forces det_blocking=[]) and plan_review_assemble_criteria -> route_criteria consume the assembled PlanContext/ticket state — so ONE shared derivation helper (module-level beside route_criteria, unit-testable) serves both steps AND the batch-runner fan-in (production_batch_runner._project_criteria -> route_criteria), which has no CLI surface. DESIGN DECISION, recorded: no --size-lines CLI flag — a transient flag cannot reach route_criteria (it takes only PlanContext, assembled from store reads), cannot reach the batch-runner caller at all, and would require amending two step-input schemas that declare additionalProperties:false (plan_review_precheck_input.schema.json / plan_review_assemble_criteria_input.schema.json); an author who wants escalation declares their blast radius in file_impact, which is also what makes the signal visible to OTHER agents. No non-test file_impact -> light advisory tier (deterministic default; B2 at Gerrit backstops with the REAL diff count, so an undeclared-blast-radius big fix is still caught before merge). When escalated, an explicit 'review-plan <bug>' includes the FULL LLM criteria set (not just BUG_TIER_CRITERIA) and stops forcing det_blocking=[] — findings can BLOCK. Small fixes keep the light advisory tier unchanged. The CLI claim-time bug exemption (rebar._commands.gates._PLAN_REVIEW_EXEMPT_TYPES, consumed by plan_review_precheck) is untouched — bugs stay claimable with no attestation.
B2: DET code-review criterion at Gerrit: commit trailer ticket is type=bug AND non-test diff >150 lines AND plan_review_status verdict is in the FLAG bucket -> BLOCKING finding teaching remediation (write fix plan into description -> review-plan -> re-push). Non-test line classification rule, load-bearing for both the gate and the backtest: a diff line is "test" iff its file path matches tests/** or conftest.py; everything else (src, scripts, workflows, docs) counts as non-test. Attestation read — CROSS-HOST, not own-env: the own-env verify wrapper (_opcert_signing.verify_opcert_record) returns foreign_key BY DESIGN for any record whose principal is not the verifying host's own env_id, so on a review-bot host distinct from the environment that ran review-plan (the NORMAL case) every legitimate attestation reads foreign_key — own-env reads (plan_review_status/claim_gate_check) are unusable for B2. Plan-review attestations are environment-signed rebar.opcert.v1 DSSE/SSHSIG op-certs (the symmetric HMAC scheme is retired — signing.py header), so B2 verifies CROSS-HOST with the op-cert trust machinery that trusted_env.verify_required_environment already composes for the completion-verifier merge gate (rebar verify-opcert, src/rebar/_commands/verify_opcert.py): read the ticket's plan-review SIGNATURE record from the store (read-only, no LLM), decode envelope + signed-bound fields via attest.opcert.opcert_from_record, load the RECORD principal's pinned keyring via attest.trusted_env.trusted_env_keyring (.rebar/trusted_environments.yaml), and verify with attest.opcert.verify_opcert (kind-bound, storage-anchor era rule) — so an op-cert from ANY pinned trusted environment can reach certified; an unpinned principal fails as mismatch (trusted_env's not-pinned arm). Freshness/lifecycle then layers on via rebar.llm.plan_review.attest.compute_validity (attest.py ~:513 — it lives under llm/plan_review, not rebar.attest) over the verify-shaped result built from the SIGNED bound fields (material_fingerprint / merged_log_commit / signed manifest), profile=DEFAULT, kind=plan-review. A record with no decodable envelope (pre-retirement legacy HMAC) is cross-host-unverifiable and classifies as unsigned. Verdict buckets, each literal attributed to its true source: (a) compute_validity's plan-review-reachable literals ('not-closed' is completion-verifier-only and excluded, stated in-test): {certified, unsigned, wrong-kind, malformed-pin, malformed-phase, stale-code, stale-head, stale-material, stale-reopened, stale-pin-drift, stale-pin-missing, unverifiable-material, incompatible-phase}; (b) the cross-host op-cert verification vocabulary (registry.Verdict / verify_signature_result.schema.json enum as emitted through verify_opcert and the scheme passthrough): {mismatch, key_not_valid_at_era, unknown_kind, unknown_scheme, invalid, unavailable}; (c) B2's own error handling {error} for read/exception paths. ACCEPTED = {certified, stale-code, stale-head} (code drift from implementing the reviewed plan is expected). FLAG = the rest of (a) + (b) minus {unavailable} — deterministic properties of the attestation itself (stale, malformed, replayed, era-invalid, or not trustworthy under the project trust root); tamper/authenticity signals are gate signal, NOT infra, and never fail open. INFRA-FAIL-OPEN = {unavailable} (verifier tooling missing on the bot host, e.g. ssh-keygen) + (c) + any verdict string in NO list (future enum growth): emit a non-blocking advisory naming the infra failure or unknown verdict, never BLOCK on infrastructure. A coverage unit test pins ACCEPTED ∪ FLAG ∪ INFRA-NAMED = (a) ∪ (b) ∪ {error} exactly — enum growth surfaces as a failing test, not silent fail-open. The 150 threshold is B2's (and the backtest's) — B1 keys on blast radius, not line count. It lives in ONE shared module-level constant in rebar imported by both its consumers — B2's review-bot criterion (the bot imports rebar) and scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py — not config-plumbed (config only if an operator-variable appears). plan_review_status (attest_gate.py) is read-only/no-LLM, callable from the review-bot checkout. Works for non-skill clients (keys only on ticket type + diff size + attestation state).

## Scope
- read-only consumers of rebar.attest.opcert / attest.trusted_env / rebar.llm.plan_review.attest.compute_validity in the review-bot criterion (no changes to those modules)
- src/rebar/llm/plan_review/workflow_ops.py precheck bug branch + the shared blast-radius derivation helper beside orchestrator.route_criteria (both steps + batch-runner key on it; NO CLI flag, NO step-input schema changes — the signal is persisted ticket state)
- orchestrator.route_criteria (~:190/:221): lift the BUG_TIER_CRITERIA restriction when the helper escalates; criteria routing for the escalated path
- review-bot DET criterion (vote pipeline)
- rebar-debug skill Phase-1-exit hook: fix-plan-to-description + review-plan for non-trivial fixes (coordinate with the debug-skill child 78f1 — writeback anchor points land there; this ticket only adds the review-plan invocation sentence)

## Testing
B1: review-plan on a bug whose file_impact names a non-test path runs the full rubric with blocking enabled (not the light tier) — asserted at BOTH seams: precheck det_blocking non-empty AND route_criteria returns the full set; no file_impact -> light tier; test-only file_impact -> light tier; batch-runner fan-in path escalates identically (route_criteria-level test); claim path unchanged (bug claims stay ungated). B2 unit tests over the predicate: bug+160 non-test lines+unsigned -> BLOCK; same with certified or stale-code or stale-head -> no finding; error/read-exception -> advisory only (fail-open); unknown verdict string -> advisory only; task ticket -> no finding; bug+40 lines -> no finding; test-vs-non-test classification cases (tests/** excluded, scripts/ counted). B2 integration: one review-bot pipeline-level test exercising the criterion end-to-end against a fixture checkout (attestation present vs absent), not just the predicate function.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Explicit review-plan <bug> escalates to the full blocking rubric when the ticket's persisted file_impact enumerates any non-test path, covering BOTH enforcement seams (precheck det_blocking + route_criteria tier) and the batch-runner fan-in; light advisory tier otherwise; claim-time exemption intact; no CLI flag and no step-input schema changes.
- [ ] Gerrit DET criterion blocks oversized bug fixes lacking a current-or-code-drifted attestation, with a teaching message.
- [ ] B2 reads the attestation CROSS-HOST (opcert_from_record -> trusted_env_keyring(record principal) -> attest.opcert.verify_opcert, the verify-opcert merge-gate's machinery — then compute_validity for freshness), NEVER via own-env plan_review_status/verify_opcert_record; a same-material op-cert signed by another PINNED trusted environment reaches ACCEPTED in a unit test.
- [ ] Verdict predicate: accepts certified/stale-code/stale-head; FLAGs compute_validity's other plan-review-reachable literals AND the cross-host op-cert failure verdicts {mismatch, key_not_valid_at_era, unknown_kind, unknown_scheme, invalid} (unpinned principal and legacy no-envelope records land in mismatch/unsigned respectively); fails OPEN (advisory, never block) only on {unavailable}/{error}/unknown-future; coverage unit test pins ACCEPTED ∪ FLAG ∪ INFRA-NAMED = compute_validity's plan-review-reachable literals (excluding completion-verifier-only 'not-closed', stated in-test) ∪ the op-cert verification vocabulary ∪ {error}.
- [ ] Non-test line classification rule stated and tested; threshold is a single named constant.
- [ ] Backtest property, exact set equality against the hand-adjudicated corpus: scripts/backtest_bugfix_size.py (one-shot, committed with the change) iterates the 113 historical bug-fix commits, applies the non-test classification rule + the shared 150 constant, and writes a JSON artifact (commit, non-test lines, flagged) recorded on this ticket; PASS iff the flagged set == the 13 commits adjudicated substantive in the planning corpus and none of the remaining 100 (which include every mechanical >150 case: rename/move/format-only/generated churn) is flagged. 'Mechanical FP' means exactly: a flagged commit outside the adjudicated-substantive 13.
- [ ] Debug-skill Phase-1-exit hook sentence landed (review-plan invocation for non-trivial fixes), coordinated with 78f1.
